title: TEACHING EXAMPLE: build the numstat integer-stream CLI from its sealed spec
note: Teaching example, not part of the benchmark. This card mirrors the shape of the scored tool_from_spec cards (e.g. gc-396 wordtally) at miniature scale: one small CLI, one sealed pytest acceptance suite, the same '^(\d+) passed' extraction. It grades in about a second, needs no network and no docker. Its reference solution ships in examples/tool_from_spec/solution/. Do not submit results for this card; it is excluded from scoring by "scored": false.
goal: Implement the numstat CLI exactly as written in assets/ex-tool_from_spec/SPEC.md, from scratch, at workspace/ex-tool_from_spec/numstat.py. The spec pins integer-token classification, two integer options with usage-error semantics (single JSON line on stdout plus exit code 2), and a deterministic JSON output contract whose totals are computed before --top truncation. Plan the behavior matrix first, implement incrementally, run the sealed acceptance suite to find divergences, and iterate until every test passes; a single naive pass typically misses the skipped-vs-filtered distinction, the tie-break direction, and the usage-error contract.
process_expectations: A plan artifact workspace/ex-tool_from_spec/plan.md exists before implementation, mapping each SPEC.md section to intended behavior.
The sealed suite was actually executed at least twice (one intermediate run allowed to be RED, one final GREEN), with command lines and summary lines logged to workspace/ex-tool_from_spec/runs.log.
Intermediate failures are tracked by test node id (failure identities, not just counts) alongside the fix applied for each.
Honest cost/failure logging: LLM spend and wall time per iteration recorded in workspace/ex-tool_from_spec/cost.json.
If any run was RED, the log shows a diagnosis -> fix -> re-run recovery cycle rather than test-file modification.
